0.body: Declare what to show. The engine decides how it looks. Declart is a declarative diagram engine. You write a TOML file describing the structure of your diagram, and Declart renders it to SVG. No layout coordinates. No styling choices. Just content.
0.title: Declart

10.body: Field Type Description kind string One of: pyramid, process, cycle, matrix, hub_spoke, venn, timeline, fishbone
10.title: Required fields

11.body: Field Type Description title string Display title rendered above the diagram. Omit to suppress.
11.title: Optional fields

12.body: Items are declared as [[items]] TOML array-of-tables. At least one item is required for all items-based kinds (pyramid, process, cycle). The matrix kind uses [[quadrants]] instead. Item order in the file is rendering order.
12.title: Item arrays

13.body: Any field not listed in a kind's spec document is forbidden. Forbidden fields cause a parse error. This includes but is not limited to: color, fill, stroke, font, size, x, y, width, height, style, class, id.
13.title: Forbidden fields

14.body: When a kind supports item-level emphasis, it uses this field: Value Meaning primary Most important item in the diagram secondary Secondary importance The engine decides visual representation. Omitting emphasis means default weight. primary: white outline stroke + bold text secondary: lighter color tint
14.breadcrumbs: Common Schema » Emphasis (shared optional item field)
14.title: Emphasis (shared optional item field)

15.body: A pyramid diagram. Items are arranged in horizontal layers from apex (top, first item) to base (bottom, last item). Conventionally used for hierarchies where importance or scarcity increases toward the apex.
15.title: Pyramid

16.body: Field Required Type Description kind yes "pyramid" Must be exactly "pyramid" title no string Title rendered above the pyramid items yes array of Item At least one item required
16.title: Fields

17.body: Field Required Type Description label yes string Text displayed in the layer emphasis no string "primary" or "secondary". See schema.
17.title: Item fields

18.body: First item (items[0]) is the apex (smallest, top). Last item (items[n-1]) is the base (widest, bottom). Layer widths increase linearly from apex to base. Apex layer degenerates to a triangle when it is the narrowest point.
18.title: Rendering rules

19.body:
kind = "pyramid"
title = "Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs" [[items]]
label = "Self-actualization" [[items]]
label = "Esteem" [[items]]
label = "Love & Belonging" [[items]]
label = "Safety" [[items]]
label = "Physiological"
19.title: Example

2.body:
# Install
cargo install declart-cli # Scaffold a starter diagram
declart init pyramid > diagram.toml # Render to SVG
declart render diagram.toml # Render to PNG
declart render diagram.toml --format png # Watch and auto-rebuild on changes
declart watch diagram.toml # Validate without rendering
declart validate diagram.toml
2.title: CLI

20.body: A process diagram. Items are arranged as sequential steps from left to right. Used for workflows, procedures, and pipelines where order matters.
20.title: Process

21.body: Field Required Type Description kind yes "process" Must be exactly "process" title no string Title rendered above the diagram items yes array of Item At least one item required
21.title: Fields

22.body: Field Required Type Description label yes string Text displayed in the step box emphasis no string "primary" or "secondary". See schema.
22.title: Item fields

23.body: Items render left to right in declaration order. Each step is a uniform box; all boxes have the same height. Directional arrows connect adjacent boxes, pointing right. Box widths are equal and fill the available canvas width. Canvas width scales to guarantee a minimum box width of 100px. Color interpolates from the first step (left) to the last step (right).
23.title: Rendering rules

24.body:
kind = "process"
title = "Software Release Pipeline" [[items]]
label = "Code Review" [[items]]
label = "Build" [[items]]
label = "Test" [[items]]
label = "Deploy" [[items]]
label = "Monitor"
24.title: Example

25.body: A cycle diagram. Items are arranged as steps in a closed loop, connected by directional arrows going clockwise. Used for recurring processes such as PDCA, feedback loops, and lifecycle models.
25.title: Cycle

26.body: Field Required Type Description kind yes "cycle" Must be exactly "cycle" title no string Title rendered above the diagram items yes array of Item At least two items required
26.title: Fields

27.body: Field Required Type Description label yes string Text displayed in the step node emphasis no string "primary" or "secondary". See schema.
27.title: Item fields

28.body: Items are arranged clockwise in a circle, starting at the top (12 o'clock). The last item connects back to the first item, forming a closed loop. Directional arrows point clockwise between adjacent nodes. Each node is a rectangular box centered on its position. Colors cycle through the apex-to-base gradient across all nodes.
28.title: Rendering rules

29.body:
kind = "cycle"
title = "PDCA Cycle" [[items]]
label = "Plan" [[items]]
label = "Do" [[items]]
label = "Check" [[items]]
label = "Act"
29.title: Example

3.body:
const declart = require('@iyulab/declart'); const svg = declart.render(`
kind = "pyramid"
title = "Maslow's Hierarchy"
[[items]]
label = "Self-actualization"
[[items]]
label = "Safety"
`);
3.title: Node.js

30.body: A two-by-two matrix diagram. Used for prioritization, strategy frameworks, and categorization with two independent axes.
30.title: Matrix 2×2

31.body: Field Required Type Description kind yes "matrix" Must be exactly "matrix" title no string Title rendered above the diagram x_axis yes string Label for the horizontal axis y_axis yes string Label for the vertical axis quadrants yes array of 4 Exactly 4 quadrants, in reading order
31.title: Fields

32.body: Field Required Type Description label yes string Text displayed in the quadrant emphasis no string "primary" or "secondary". See schema.
32.title: Quadrant fields

33.body: Quadrants are declared in reading order (left-to-right, top-to-bottom): Top-left (high Y, low X) Top-right (high Y, high X) Bottom-left (low Y, low X) Bottom-right (low Y, high X)
33.title: Quadrant order

34.body: The diagram is a 2×2 grid divided by a horizontal and vertical axis line. Each quadrant occupies one cell of the grid and displays its label centered. x_axis is rendered below the horizontal center line. y_axis is rendered to the left of the vertical center line, rotated 90°. Exactly 4 quadrants are required; more or fewer is a parse error.
34.title: Rendering rules

35.body:
kind = "matrix"
title = "Eisenhower Matrix"
x_axis = "Importance"
y_axis = "Urgency" [[quadrants]]
label = "Do First" [[quadrants]]
label = "Schedule" [[quadrants]]
label = "Delegate" [[quadrants]]
label = "Eliminate"
35.title: Example

36.body: A hub-and-spoke diagram. A central node radiates connections to surrounding spoke nodes. Used for showing a central concept with related elements, or a hub with connected services.
36.title: Hub-and-Spoke

37.body: Field Required Type Description kind yes "hub_spoke" Must be exactly "hub_spoke" title no string Title rendered above the diagram center yes string Label for the central hub node spokes yes array of Spoke At least one spoke required
37.title: Fields

38.body: Field Required Type Description label yes string Text displayed in the spoke node emphasis no string "primary" or "secondary". See schema.
38.title: Spoke fields

39.body: The center node is rendered at the center of the diagram. Spoke nodes are arranged evenly around the center in a circle. Lines connect the center node to each spoke node. The center node is visually distinguished from spoke nodes (larger, different color). Spoke nodes use the base color; the center uses the apex color.
39.title: Rendering rules

41.body: A Venn diagram. Two or three overlapping circles represent sets. Intersection regions may be labeled. Used for showing set relationships, similarities, and differences.
41.title: Venn

42.body: Field Required Type Description kind yes "venn" Must be exactly "venn" title no string Title rendered above the diagram sets yes array of Set 2 or 3 sets required intersections no array of Intersection Labeled regions in the overlap areas
42.title: Fields

43.body: Field Required Type Description label yes string Name of the set
43.title: Set fields

44.body: Field Required Type Description sets yes array of string Set labels identifying which overlap region this labels label yes string Text displayed in the overlap region
44.title: Intersection fields

45.body: Circles are arranged to overlap: two sets side-by-side; three sets in a triangle. Each circle is rendered with partial opacity so overlaps are visible. Set labels appear near the outer edge of each circle (non-overlapping region). Intersection labels appear in the center of the overlap region. Exactly 2 or 3 sets are required; other counts are a parse error.
45.title: Rendering rules

46.body:
kind = "venn"
title = "Skills Overlap" [[sets]]
label = "Design" [[sets]]
label = "Engineering" [[intersections]]
sets = ["Design", "Engineering"]
label = "UX Engineering"
46.title: Example

47.body: A timeline diagram. Events are placed along a horizontal axis at positions proportional to their dates. Used for project histories, product roadmaps, and chronological narratives.
47.title: Timeline

48.body: Field Required Type Description kind yes "timeline" Must be exactly "timeline" title no string Title rendered above the diagram events yes array of Event At least two events required
48.title: Fields

49.body: Field Required Type Description date yes string Date in ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD label yes string Text displayed above or below the event marker
49.title: Event fields

50.body: Events are sorted by date and placed along a horizontal axis. The horizontal position of each event is proportional to its date within the overall date range. Event labels alternate above and below the axis to reduce overlap. The date string is displayed below each event marker. At least two events are required to establish a time range.
50.title: Rendering rules

52.body: A fishbone (Ishikawa) cause-and-effect diagram. A central spine leads to an effect. Causes branch off the spine; each cause may have sub-causes. Used for root cause analysis and structured problem decomposition.
52.title: Fishbone (Ishikawa)

53.body: Field Required Type Description kind yes "fishbone" Must be exactly "fishbone" title no string Title rendered above the diagram effect yes string Label for the effect (right end of the spine) causes yes array of Cause At least two causes required
53.title: Fields

54.body: Field Required Type Description label yes string Label displayed at the branch head items no array of Item Sub-causes branching off this cause
54.title: Cause fields

55.body: Field Required Type Description label yes string Text displayed on the sub-cause line
55.title: Item fields (sub-cause)

56.body: The spine is a horizontal line from left to right. The effect box is at the right end of the spine. Causes alternate above and below the spine, evenly spaced. Each cause is represented by a diagonal branch line ending in a labeled box. Sub-causes are shorter branches off the cause branch. At least two causes are required.
56.title: Rendering rules

title = "Website Performance Issues" effect = "Slow Page Load" [[causes]]
label = "Server" [[causes.items]]

label = "Memory limits" [[causes]]
label = "Network" [[causes.items]]
label = "Bandwidth" [[causes]]
label = "Code" [[causes]]
label = "Database" [[causes.items]]
label = "Slow queries"
57.title: Example

6.body: See Principles for the full design rationale. The key idea: declarations express what exists, not how it looks. The engine owns visual decisions.
6.title: Design Philosophy

7.body: → Open the Declart Playground — no installation required Edit TOML declarations and see your diagrams rendered live in the browser. All 8 diagram kinds are available, with default and monochrome themes. Note: The playground requires HTTP to load the WASM module. Use mdbook serve docs/ for local testing rather than opening the file directly.
7.title: Interactive Playground

8.body: These principles govern every declaration file format in Declart, across all diagram kinds and all implementations. Design exclusion. Declaration files contain no visual information: no colors, coordinates, fonts, sizes, margins, or layout hints. These are the engine's domain. Semantics only. Fields express meaning, not appearance. emphasis: primary is allowed; color: red is not. The engine decides how emphasis looks. LLM-predictable. Field names are single English words. Structure is flat or exactly one level deep ([[items]]). A language model must be able to generate a correct declaration without examples. Minimal and concise. Each kind defines only its required fields. Optional fields are added only when proven necessary across multiple use cases. When in doubt, leave it out. One representation per kind. There is exactly one way to express each diagram. No aliases, no alternate structures, no flags that change interpretation. Two valid declarations that express the same diagram must be byte-for-byte identical except for whitespace.
8.title: Declart Grammar Principles
